executive_summary: Approve a thin Chrome Manifest V3 side-panel extension connected to a durable local companion through native messaging, subject to Sina's explicit approval of the decision register before implementation. The local companion should own SQLite state, exchange files, hashes, validation, recovery, and project-completion records; the extension should own only visible Go/Done interaction and transient browser coordination; Codex should remain the project manager, semantic validator, and integrator; and the user should remain the person who attaches files, presses ChatGPT Send, reviews output, downloads files, and selects them for collection. The current manual protocol is a strong evidence and fallback foundation but lacks a durable state machine, idempotency, exact package digest, project-level completion graph, concurrency model, security/privacy gate, and implemented bridge. Current OpenAI Terms prohibit automatic/programmatic extraction of data or output, so the recommended baseline does not scrape the response page or use private endpoints: Done opens a native user-controlled file picker after the user downloads files normally. The two attached Markdown artifacts provide the complete candidate design and a dependency-ordered implementation/testing roadmap; no code or executable implementation has been created in this call.

work_performed.summary: Reconstructed the current manual workflow from every uploaded file, separated documented behavior from inference, identified retained strengths, and produced a prioritized gap/disposition audit. The audit highlights the missing durable lifecycle, weak request-response byte binding, absent project-completion model, defense-specific universal path, singleton active request, schema integrity gaps, privacy/secret omissions, filename ambiguity, and the absence of an implemented bridge/test harness.

Compared four feasible architectures—extension-only, thin extension plus native companion, extension plus loopback service, and full browser automation/RPA—using an explicit weighted matrix covering reliability, security, maintainability, UI resilience, portability, effort, testability, and user control. Recommended the native-messaging hybrid and documented technology, permission, trust, and policy boundaries with current primary-source citations.

Designed the complete Prepare-to-Go-to-Done-to-Validated-to-Integrated lifecycle, canonical states, transition contract, idempotency and retry semantics, crash/duplicate/stale/concurrency behavior, durable SQLite/event/file model, v3 data contracts, and read-only legacy migration strategy.

Defined layered request, authorization, collection, structural, semantic, integration, and whole-project completion gates; documented invariants, observability, a failure taxonomy, recovery playbooks, and a threat model covering extension, native host, filesystem, browser session, model output, policy, privacy, and operational risks.

Created a phased implementation and verification roadmap beginning with a smallest coherent end-to-end vertical slice. Every phase specifies scope, outputs, prerequisites, risks, automated/manual tests, acceptance evidence, exit criteria, rollback, and deferrals; the roadmap includes a consolidated test matrix, release gates, failure injection, UAT, and explicit preservation of the manual workflow.

question_responses.answer: The current system already provides a universal reasoning gate, bounded task requests, ranked source authority, timestamped isolated request/response exchanges, a mandatory schema-constrained response attachment and artifact manifest, explicit manual user transport, Codex validation, advisory treatment of Web output, and retained exchange evidence. It does not yet provide the upgraded product: there is no extension or companion, durable lifecycle, idempotency, crash recovery, exact package digest, safe response collection mechanism, concurrent-project model, revision lineage, project requirement/completion graph, sensitivity gate, or comprehensive test harness. Several current contracts validate JSON shape but cannot prove that a COMPLETE response contains every requested ID/artifact or corresponds to the exact uploaded bytes.
question_responses.reasoning_summary: The working manual protocol is not a failed prototype; it is a strong fallback and evidence format. The highest-priority defects are the missing durable operational model and weak byte-level request/response binding. Features such as the extension and completion dashboard are genuinely absent rather than defective. The design retains the manual evidence principles while adding state, identity, safety, and recovery.

question_responses.answer: The best balance is a thin MV3 side-panel extension plus a local companion reached through Chrome native messaging. The extension presents user-visible Go/Done interaction and transient tab coordination; the companion owns SQLite state, files, hashes, validators, recovery, and native dialogs. This scores 435/500 (87%) in the design matrix, ahead of a loopback-service hybrid at 400/500, extension-only at 290/500, and full browser automation at 145/500. Native messaging avoids a listening local port, pins access to explicit extension origins, and allows file operations to remain outside the fragile Web UI. The baseline has no response-DOM dependency.
question_responses.reasoning_summary: Extension-only storage and service-worker lifecycle are insufficient for durable filesystem-backed project management. A loopback service is viable but adds local network, CSRF/token, CORS, firewall, and port risks. Full RPA is brittle, weakens user control, exposes authentication, and conflicts with current restrictions on programmatic output extraction. Native messaging has installation cost but the strongest trust boundary and recovery/testability profile for Sina's Windows/Chrome environment.

question_responses.answer: The extension should display the next call, exact outgoing files and hashes, expected outputs, privacy/staleness warnings, Go/Done/recovery controls, and transient tab status. It may open/focus ChatGPT, copy the prompt after a user click, and ask the companion to reveal the frozen request folder or open the response picker. The companion should own package creation, approved-root path access, hashing, SQLite transactions, locks, idempotency, native dialogs, collection, quarantine, schema/artifact validation, event logs, and reconciliation. Codex should own task decomposition, authority, semantic validation, correction decisions, integration, and completion. The user must attach files, use ChatGPT Send, review the answer, download files through normal controls, select files on Done, and make consequential approvals. The extension must not read cookies, scrape the response, use private endpoints, click Send, silently retry, or collect unrelated browsing/download content.
question_responses.reasoning_summary: Least privilege requires browser code to hold as little file/state authority as possible and requires the user to remain the actual service operator. The side panel is well suited to a visible companion UI, while native messaging moves privileged local operations to a tightly registered host. Current Chrome guidance favors optional/minimum permissions and treats content-script messages as untrusted.

question_responses.answer: Use canonical per-call states DRAFT, PACKAGING, READY, HANDOFF_ACTIVE, optional AWAITING_RESPONSE, COLLECTING, COLLECTED, VALIDATING, NEEDS_CORRECTION, ACCEPTED, INTEGRATING, INTEGRATED, REJECTED, FAILED, CANCELLED, and STALE; model PAUSED as a flag retaining paused_from_state. Every transition must record actor, expected prior state/version, preconditions, idempotency key, atomic side effects, event evidence, result state/version, retry class, and user-visible outcome. SQLite is the transactional operational index, the exchange filesystem is durable byte evidence, CALL_STATE is a materialized view, and EVENTS.jsonl is a portable event mirror. New v3 manifests/contracts add project_id, call_id, lineage, package manifest, canonical request digest, complete file metadata, exact expected outputs, conditional completion, response digest echo, and structured validation reports. Legacy v2 exchanges remain byte-for-byte read-only under a dual validator/importer.
question_responses.reasoning_summary: A state label alone is insufficient; resumability and idempotency require compare-and-swap state versions, unique command keys, per-call locks, transactional events, staged filesystem writes, and deterministic reconciliation. The filesystem and database have complementary roles and must not become silent competing authorities. A new contract version is safer than stretching v2 without reliable conditional semantics.

question_responses.answer: Reliable collection should begin only after the user reviews ChatGPT's answer and downloads the required files through normal controls. On Done, the local companion opens a visible native multi-file picker; the user selects the exact files. The companion copies them into exchange-local staging, checks stability, hashes and atomically stores them, validates the expected main filename/schema/request ID, checks v3 call ID and request digest when available, cross-checks every artifact manifest entry and hash, and quarantines missing/wrong/partial/ambiguous candidates. It never reads the ChatGPT response DOM, network traffic, cookies, or unrelated downloads. Browser-uniquified filenames are normalized only after content/schema binding and with the original name recorded.
question_responses.reasoning_summary: Explicit user selection provides the strongest protection against collecting unrelated page or download content and avoids the broad Chrome downloads permission. Native selection retains real local paths and supports large files without sending file bytes over the size-limited native-messaging channel. Request ID plus canonical package digest provides strong call association for v3; legacy v2 remains weaker and requires explicit review.

question_responses.answer: Use six distinct gates: request eligibility and immutable package validation; Go disclosure/authorization; user-selected collection; structural response validation; Codex semantic/authority validation; and integration/project-completion validation. A response cannot be Accepted unless request/call/digest identity, schema, exact work/question/artifact ID coverage, artifact files/hashes, source requirements, and acceptance criteria pass. A structurally valid response remains advisory until Codex verifies important claims and conflicts. Missing or incorrect work creates a linked correction/revision call; it never silently advances. Integrated and Project Complete remain separate from Accepted.
question_responses.reasoning_summary: The current schemas provide useful shape validation but lack cross-field and cross-file invariants. Layering deterministic and intellectual checks prevents both malformed packages and plausible but wrong model output from being mistaken for completion. The project requirement graph prevents call count or response presence from becoming a completion proxy.

question_responses.answer: Principal threats are prohibited/fragile browser automation, compromised extension or content-script messages, excessive permissions, local path traversal/reparse points, native-host spoofing/replay, accidental secret upload, cross-call response mix-up, malicious model files/JSON, UI change, worker/browser termination, duplicate/concurrent actions, inaccurate model output, unsuitable ChatGPT retention/training settings, state loss/disk failure, sensitive logs, auth theft, dependency compromise, and stale requests. Mandatory first-use controls include no scraping/private endpoints/cookie access; exact native allowed_origins; minimum extension permissions; strict message schemas; approved filesystem roots and link/path rejection; secret/sensitivity disclosure; request digests and hashes; untrusted-data parsing limits; transactional/idempotent state; metadata-only logs; manual fallback; and explicit user Send/download/Done selection.
question_responses.reasoning_summary: The most dangerous failures are silent: sending undisclosed files, collecting unrelated output, binding the wrong response, accepting unvalidated model work, or advancing state after an ambiguous crash. Controls therefore fail closed and preserve evidence. Residual risk remains from provider changes, model error, local-account compromise, scanner false negatives, and platform vulnerabilities; the design does not claim perfect security.

question_responses.answer: After a read-only Phase 0 baseline and decision gate, Codex should implement one vertical slice: local SQLite/event core, strict native-messaging bridge, minimal side panel, exact disclosure, idempotent Go, prompt-copy/folder-reveal assistance, manual ChatGPT Send/download, Done-triggered native file selection, v2 response/artifact validation, restart recovery, quarantine, and manual fallback. Expansion requires 100% deterministic state/contract/path/security tests, failure injection at every persistence boundary, mock-browser extension tests, at least one non-sensitive real UAT call, no unresolved critical/major security issue, unchanged legacy fixtures, successful manual fallback, and Sina's explicit acceptance.
question_responses.reasoning_summary: This slice proves both trust boundaries and end-to-end value without depending on v3 contracts, project intelligence, or DOM automation. Building a headless state engine alone would not validate Go/Done usability; building page automation first would increase risk before durable identity/recovery exists. The roadmap therefore places decisions and golden fixtures first, then a minimal complete path, then state/contract hardening, project completion, optional input assist, and distribution.

question_responses.answer: Nine consequential choices remain: (1) safe automation ceiling, with manual Send/download baseline recommended; (2) Done collection, with native user file selection recommended over downloads monitoring; (3) native messaging versus loopback, with native messaging recommended; (4) v3 contracts versus stretching v2, with v3 plus dual validation recommended; (5) per-project exchange root versus universal docs/Defense, with configurable roots and preserved legacy recommended; (6) new chat per call versus reused/project chat, with new chat by default; (7) sensitive-call mode among normal, Temporary Chat, and do-not-send, chosen per call; (8) pilot distribution, beginning with single-user development then signed private release; and (9) local retention/clipboard defaults, with project-defined retention and user-click clipboard writing. Decisions 1–5 are blocking before implementation beyond baseline inventory.
question_responses.reasoning_summary: These decisions materially change permissions, policy exposure, privacy, migration cost, hidden context, installer complexity, and user action count. They cannot be silently converted from design assumptions into product requirements. The recommendation optimizes safety and reversibility first while leaving optional convenience behind explicit later gates.

findings.finding: The upgraded brief's phrase 'gather the response' is ambiguous; current OpenAI Terms prohibit automatic/programmatic extraction of data or output.
findings.why_it_matters: A naïve response scraper or private-endpoint integration could violate service rules, collect unrelated content, expose authentication, and make the product unsafe.
findings.recommended_action: Keep Send, review, and download as direct user actions; make Done invoke an explicit native file picker; prohibit response DOM/network scraping and private endpoints.

findings.finding: The current protocol has no authoritative transition model, event log, state version, idempotency key, lock, or crash-recovery semantics.
findings.why_it_matters: Duplicate actions, browser restarts, and concurrent projects can create ambiguous or contradictory state and duplicate intellectual calls.
findings.recommended_action: Implement SQLite transactions, per-call state/version, idempotent commands, locks, staged filesystem commits, and rebuildable events before convenience automation.

findings.finding: A matching request_id does not bind a response to the exact bytes actually disclosed and uploaded because the current request has no canonical package digest/file hashes.
findings.why_it_matters: A valid-looking response may belong to a stale, modified, or different package.
findings.recommended_action: Create PACKAGE_MANIFEST.json with per-file hashes and an RFC-8785-canonical request_digest; require v3 responses to echo it.

findings.finding: The brief defines project completion, but no supplied data model represents requirements, dependencies, accepted evidence, integration, blockers, or final audit.
findings.why_it_matters: The system cannot prove that the original objective is complete and may confuse returned calls with completed work.
findings.recommended_action: Add project/requirement/evidence/integration/final-audit records and derive completion only from mandatory invariants.

findings.finding: Current schemas validate shape but not exact requested-ID coverage, conditional COMPLETE semantics, artifact hash presence, direct Web-source metadata, or strong provenance.
findings.why_it_matters: A schema-valid response can still omit required work/artifacts or make unverifiable self-assertions.
findings.recommended_action: Introduce v3 conditional contracts and independent cross-file validation while retaining v2 validators for legacy exchanges.

findings.finding: The universal gate is hard-coded under docs/Defense and the protocol exposes one active_request slot.
findings.why_it_matters: Non-defense projects and multiple ready/paused calls cannot be represented safely.
findings.recommended_action: Use configurable per-project exchange roots and queryable per-call records; preserve the historical defense path read-only.

findings.finding: An extension that monitors all downloads or has persistent ChatGPT/all-sites access would exceed the safe baseline and increase compromise impact.
findings.why_it_matters: Downloads metadata can include absolute local paths and broad page access can expose unrelated browsing data.
findings.recommended_action: Limit baseline permissions to sidePanel, nativeMessaging, and preference storage; use a native user picker and gate any optional page access separately.

findings.finding: The current package contract has no sensitivity classification, secret scan, explicit override, data-control reminder, or retention decision.
findings.why_it_matters: Sensitive files or credentials can be sent without a deliberate privacy decision, and local/provider retention may be unsuitable.
findings.recommended_action: Add secret/sensitivity preflight, exact disclosure, explicit override evidence, chat-mode/data-control notice, metadata-only logs, and project-defined local retention.

findings.finding: Transport and browser duplicate suffixes can change filenames, and the current contract does not record original versus normalized names.
findings.why_it_matters: Manual renaming can attach the wrong file or break artifact accounting.
findings.recommended_action: Bind by call/digest/schema/hash, record both names, normalize only after unambiguous validation, and quarantine conflicts.

findings.finding: No extension, companion, installer, compatibility probe, mocked browser surface, failure injection, or recovery test currently exists.
findings.why_it_matters: The desired Go/Done behavior and reliability remain unproven.
findings.recommended_action: Build the Phase 1 vertical slice only after the decision/baseline phase, and require deterministic, failure-injection, mock-browser, real UAT, and manual-fallback evidence.

findings.finding: Schema validity and artifact presence cannot establish intellectual correctness.
findings.why_it_matters: A well-formed output can invent facts, conflict with authority, or answer the wrong question.
findings.recommended_action: Keep Codex semantic/authority validation, critic/revision workflows, and user acceptance separate from deterministic validation.

findings.finding: The current example records useful hashes and timestamps but no standardized event/failure taxonomy or content-minimizing diagnostic contract.
findings.why_it_matters: Recovery and support can become guesswork or leak sensitive prompt/output content.
findings.recommended_action: Adopt metadata-only structured events, health checks, validator versions, failure codes, redaction, and local-only metrics.

recommendations: Approve the thin MV3 side-panel plus native-messaging local companion as the target architecture.
Interpret Go as visible authorization and preparation, not hidden Send; keep ChatGPT's native Send under direct user control.
Implement Done as explicit native file selection after the user downloads files normally; do not scrape the response page or monitor unrelated downloads.
Make the companion the durable authority using SQLite transactions plus immutable exchange evidence; keep the extension non-authoritative.
Freeze each request with a complete package manifest and canonical request digest, and require v3 response binding to that digest.
Introduce v3 request/response/manifest/validation contracts for new calls while preserving v2 exchanges byte-for-byte and validating both versions.
Represent project requirements, call dependencies, acceptance, integration, blockers, final audit, and user approval so project completion is provable.
Adopt the baseline permission budget with no downloads, cookies, debugger, all-sites, persistent ChatGPT host, or content-script access.
Implement Phase 0 and the Phase 1 vertical slice before any optional ChatGPT composer assistance.
Keep the manual protocol available at every phase and roll back immediately on silent send/collection, wrong-call acceptance, state irreconcilability, or policy conflict.
Require Sina's explicit approval of the decision register before implementation beyond read-only baseline work.
Re-check current OpenAI terms, ChatGPT limits/data controls, Chrome APIs, and extension policies before each release that expands permissions or automation.

limitations: This response is an architecture and implementation-planning review only; no repository code, Chrome extension, native host, installer, state database, or executable system was created or tested.

The actual F1D repository and its complete exchange history were not included; migration details are based on the supplied protocol, schemas, instructions, and one operational example and must be verified read-only in Phase 0.

No automated or live browser interaction with Sina's authenticated ChatGPT account was performed. Exact current UI details, native picker focus behavior, prompt-copy behavior, and supported ChatGPT destination flow require a non-sensitive manual prototype.

Current OpenAI Terms were interpreted conservatively to prohibit response DOM/network extraction; this is an architectural risk judgment, not legal advice. Policies can change and must be re-reviewed before release.
ChatGPT upload limits, plan behavior, UI, Chrome APIs, and extension policies are time-sensitive. Web claims were verified on 2026-07-14 and may require later refresh.
Hashes provide byte-integrity evidence, not author authentication or protection against a fully compromised local account.
Secret scanning, schema validation, hashing, and model review reduce but cannot eliminate sensitive-data leakage, malicious-file risk, or intellectual error.
